Maintenance Report — MNT-0151-002

Asset: WELL-0151 (NE-08 Well 151, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 04 Mar 2023 08:00 · Finished: 15 Mar 2023 02:00 · Well stopped for this job: 258 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0151-0020 on 2023-03-02 Report written: 17 Mar 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw a thin film of oil on the wellhead. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0151-0020 showed the wellhead at 12.4 °C with the air at 8.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Normal packing wear.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0151-009

Asset: WELL-0151 (NE-08 Well 151, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: separator Work started: 10 May 2024 08:00 · Finished: 21 May 2024 16:00 · Well stopped for this job: 272 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price, Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0151-0080 on 2024-05-09 Report written: 21 May 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the separator high-level alarm stayed on. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0151-0080 showed the wellhead at 34.3 °C with the air at 29.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The level controller had failed. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

  1. Isolated and depressurised the separator.
  2. Replaced the level controller.
  3. Calibrated the controller and tested the dump valve.

Summary of the fix: replaced level controller.

Testing and return to service

Cycled the separator three times; level control worked correctly. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0151-017

Asset: WELL-0151 (NE-08 Well 151, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 22 Aug 2025 08:00 · Finished: 23 Aug 2025 03:00 · Well stopped for this job: 19 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0151-0147 on 2025-08-21 Report written: 23 Aug 2025

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0151-0147 at 14:00 on 2025-08-21 found crude oil on the pad: about 4.0% of the pad area, estimated 1.8 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.9 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 326 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 261 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.4 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0151-017 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.63% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0151-023

Asset: WELL-0151 (NE-08 Well 151, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: rod string Work started: 28 Aug 2026 08:00 · Finished: 07 Sep 2026 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 252 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0151-0197 on 2026-08-27 Report written: 09 Sep 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0151-0197 showed the wellhead at 42.3 °C with the air at 33.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 8 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Sucker rods3,297
Rod couplings824
Fishing tool rental1,374
Labour (company crew)5,808
Total11,303

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail
WS-01MetMeeting held and recorded
WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 1 ppm
WS-07MetWritten 2 days after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Consider corrosion inhibitor treatment for this well.
  • Keep the recovered rod for failure analysis.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0151-026

Asset: WELL-0151 (NE-08 Well 151, T350, Northeast Block 8) Equipment: flowline Work started: 04 Oct 2026 08:00 · Finished: 06 Oct 2026 00:00 · Well stopped for this job: 40 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0151-0202 on 2026-10-01 Report written: 07 Oct 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0151-0202 showed the wellhead at 33.4 °C with the air at 28.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line.

Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 326 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 261 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0151-026 (WS-06).
